angle: The exec's argument and the reply to it

sources.title: Crimson Desert Exec Explains The Gulf Between The Mid Review Scores And The 6 Million Sales
A Crimson Desert exec thinks critic review scores were lower because they didn't have enough time to play it, and boy oh boy I wonder whose fault that is

claims.claim: Kotaku published a piece headlined: Crimson Desert Exec Explains The Gulf Between The Mid Review Scores And The 6 Million Sales
claims.evidence: Launch-day patches were part of the problem

claims.claim: Rock Paper Shotgun published a piece headlined: A Crimson Desert exec thinks critic review scores were lower because they didn't have enough time to play it, and boy oh boy I wonder whose fault that is
claims.evidence: Crimson Desert looks like a perfectly fine game. I've not played it, and I don't intend to, so my perspective is based predominantly on trailers and reviews from my industry peers. Which, as it happens, also generally seemed to reach a consensus of "yeah, it's fine." Sibling site European Gamer certainly seemed to think so , as did others. But if you ask the European CEO of developer Pearl Abyss L

claims.claim: Pearl Abyss Europe chief executive Lybee Park told The Game Business that critics reviewed a build that was not the same as the launch version.
claims.quote: They had to play the build that is not the exact same version as the launch game.

claims.claim: Park said critics had limited time and tend to follow the main quest line, while the game's appeal is spread across its world.
claims.quote: our unique charm is spread all over our in-game world

claims.claim: Crimson Desert has a 77 on Metacritic and has sold 6 million copies, a figure Pearl Abyss confirmed.
claims.evidence: Kotaku: 77 on Metacritic, 6 million sales milestone; correction notes Pearl Abyss confirmed 6 million.

claims.claim: Critics praised the open world and combat but found the story weak, while the game rose to the top of the Steam charts.
claims.evidence: Kotaku summarises critical and player reception.

claims.claim: Kotaku notes some reviewers played for more than 100 hours before publishing.
claims.evidence: Kotaku: some played over 100 hours before delivering their assessments.

claims.claim: The game received a day-one patch and a large first-week update that overhauled systems including the inventory limits that had frustrated reviewers.
claims.evidence: Kotaku: day-one patch and big update in its first week, including inventory limitations.

claims.claim: The Charting the Unknown DLC arrives on 29 October.
claims.evidence: Kotaku: new DLC arrives on October 29.

claims.claim: Rock Paper Shotgun's writer accepts that critics are often short of time but asks whose fault that is, pointing at the developer.
claims.evidence: RPS: whose fault is it that critics had such little time?

claims.claim: Rock Paper Shotgun argues a critic's job differs from a player's experience, and that an average review is not a verdict on people who enjoy a game.
claims.evidence: RPS on the difference between what a critic does and what the average person does.

claims.claim: Kotaku argues sales and quality need not correlate, in games as in film.
claims.evidence: Kotaku: no necessary correlation between sales and quality.
